name: P values

subjectOf.text: Across an array of robustness tests, the requirements introduced by the Dodd-Frank Act create no significant effect on private fund performance, with all reported RD p-values above the 5% level.
subjectOf.abstract: Using an array of robustness tests validating our RD results, Figures 3-7 suggest that the requirements introduced by the Dodd-Frank Act create no significant effect on private fund performance. The P-values for all RD results in Table 6 are above the 5% level and confirm our finding of no effect.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Private Fund Performance  – Evidence from 2010 – 2015 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2816408

subjectOf.text: A substrate was declared procedure-invalid by the operator before any run or reading, with no pre-run rule fired and no written reason recorded, and its nine registered tests stand at a p-value of one with no other label, so the filter is tested on one substrate, a two-dimensional mixture with simulated validators.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: The paper draws no inference from the invalidated substrate.
The declaration is one of two departures from the frozen procedure that the paper discloses.

subjectOf.text: A contrast is superior when its Holm-adjusted p-value is below 0.05, its 95 percent interval lies above zero, and its point estimate is at least 0.10; it is negative when the adjusted p-value is below 0.05 and the interval lies below zero, a substantive null when its 90 percent interval lies within plus or minus that margin, and inconclusive otherwise.

This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: The unit of analysis is the seed, and every contrast is a paired seed-level difference within a validator family.
The effect sizes were fixed by the operator before any pilot.
